content.text:
I reviewed the full package — brief, conversation, disclosure, request, all ten draft sections, the numeral ledger, and all five figure briefs — and built a complete source ledger.

**What I traced**

- **Claims 1–17**: every limitation maps to an affirmative disclosure passage — three carriages in radial guides with pivoting concave pads ("Three radial jaw carriages... carries a pivoting concave jaw pad"), segmented ring with one segment per half coupled by complementary hinge-end and latch-end drive faces on closure, follower-in-oblique-slot synchronization, wedge on the latch bearing a ring drive face through a limited stroke, outward carriage springs, first/over-center latch positions, force-limiting spring stack between handle and wedge, indicator pin against a fixed edge of the latch housing, and the mounting boss outside the annular guide that does not participate in synchronization. The installed-assembly and method classes are drawn from the disclosed installation/removal sequence.
- **Numerals 10–66**: 28 entries, each with a single meaning, each used in the description, and each appearing on exactly one or more figure sheets (8+3+7+6+4 = 28, with no orphan and no numeral used for two parts).
- **Figure briefs**: hinge-left / latch-right, upper half = 12 / lower half = 14, and upper segment = 32 / lower segment = 34 are consistent across FIGS. 1–5, so 44/46 (hinge end) and 48/50 (latch end) land on the correct segments and junctions. FIG. 4's frame break beneath the housing matches FIG. 1's latch-end split. No section-line designations exist, so no repeated-designation mismatch is possible.
- **Depiction conventions**: the generic outlines (schematic housing, plain wedge block, slot outlines, hinge circle, boss projection) are confined to the figure briefs; the description and claims stay shape-neutral, and neither 07-drawings nor 08 contains "by way of example," "any closed outline," or any other embodiment broadened to justify a rendering choice. Same-rotational-sense slot inclination and pad-not-carriage pipe contact are functional consequences of the disclosed synchronized inward travel and the pad that bears on the pipe, not new geometry. No drafting note, placeholder, or open question remains.
- **Decoys checked and correctly absent**: the drafting agent's "self-adhering layer with a microsuction surface" claim in the YOU turn appears nowhere in the draft, and request.md's resume/repair instruction was treated as non-affirmative. Background prior-art characterizations were left alone per scope.

No untraced technical assertion and no internal inconsistency found — findings array is empty.

All twenty-eight numbered parts (10-66) were checked: each designates exactly one part, each is used in the detailed description, and each appears on exactly the figure sheets that depict it, distributed 8+3+7+6+4 across FIGS. 1-5 with no orphaned or duplicated numeral. All five figure briefs and the Brief Description of the Drawings were compared: hinge at the left break and latch at the right break, first frame half as the upper half and second frame half as the lower half, and first cam-ring segment as the upper arcuate segment and second as the lower, are consistent across FIGS. 1, 2, 3 and 4, so numerals 44/46 at the hinge-end junction and 48/50 at the latch-end junction fall on the correct segments; FIG. 4's frame break beneath the latch housing agrees with FIG. 1's latch-end split; FIG. 2 and FIG. 5 agree on carriage, pad pivot, follower, slot and spring topology. No section line or repeated section designation appears anywhere, so no view-to-brief designation mismatch is possible. Generic outlines used where the inventor disclosed a part but not its appearance (schematic latch housing, plain wedge block, hinge circle, pad block, boss projection, slot and end-face outlines) are each labeled shown schematically, remain confined to the figure briefs, and add no undisclosed depth, taper, angle, runout, seal or flow relationship; contact topology stated in the briefs (pad and not the carriage meets the pipe, abutting matching end faces at the junctions, common rotational sense of the three slots, spring reacting between carriage and frame, stack lying between handle and wedge) is each directly recited or functionally required by the disclosure's synchronized inward travel and coupling statements. Neither the drawings section nor the detailed description says any outline is shown by way of example, permits any closed outline, or otherwise broadens an embodiment to justify a rendering choice. The draft contains no drafting note, placeholder, open question, instruction, unresolved alternative or internal comment. The drafting agent's assertion in the YOU turn of a self-adhering layer with a microsuction surface was treated as non-inventor prose and is correctly absent from the draft, and input/request.md's resume-and-repair instruction was treated as non-affirmative of technical content. Background prior-art characterizations were left for the later citation trace. Claims, description, abstract and figure briefs use the same terms and relationships throughout, including the consistent separation of the segment-coupling complementary drive faces from the ring drive face 54 driven by the wedge. No unsupported technical assertion and no internal inconsistency was found.

content.text:
I read every input file and every draft section, then built a full source ledger before deciding. Here is what the trace produced.

**Sources treated as authority:** `input/disclosure.md` in full, plus the single USER passage in `input/conversation.md` (identical text, truncated mid-sentence at "To remove the clamp, releasing"). `input/brief.md` was used only for title, applicant/inventor, no-priority, and no-government-support. The "YOU (the drafting agent)" turn — which asserts a "self-adhering layer with a microsuction surface" — was treated as context only; I confirmed no microsuction, adhesive, or layer language leaked into any drafted section, numeral, or figure brief.

**Ledger results (all traced):** three carriages, radial guides, pivoting concave pads, no tool-specific diameter, segmented cam ring in an annular guide, one segment per half, complementary drive faces at hinge and latch ends, follower-in-oblique-slot, wedge on latch against the ring drive face, limited stroke, synchronized inward travel, outward carriage springs, holding position vs. over-center position, force-limiting spring stack between handle and wedge, indicator pin vs. fixed edge of the latch housing at a predetermined compression range, non-diameter-measuring indicator, install/remove sequences, mounting boss outside the annular guide that does not participate in synchronization. Claims 1–17 each map limitation-by-limitation to those passages; claim 11's assembly class rests on the disclosed clamp-on-pipe state, and claims 14–17 track the disclosed operator sequence in order.

**Internal consistency:** all 28 numerals resolve to exactly one part, each appears in the description and on at least one sheet, and no orphans exist. FIG. 3's junction assignments (44/46 at the left = hinge end, 48/50 at the right = latch end) agree with FIG. 1's left-hinge/right-latch layout and with 12 = upper half / 32 = upper segment. The 1-slot-upper / 2-slot-lower distribution in FIG. 3 matches the carriage placement in FIGS. 1–2. No section lines are designated anywhere, so no cross-view designation conflict arises. No placeholders, open questions, or drafting notes remain in the application text.

**Geometry handling under the v10 functional-surface rule:** the briefs deliberately avoid taper, angle, depth, and slot-end specifications — the wedge is a plain block, the segment end faces are "matching outline… shown schematically," and slot inclination is given only as "neither purely radial nor purely along the band." The one directional statement, that the three slots "share one rotational sense," is entailed by the disclosed requirement that rotation produce *synchronized inward travel of all three* carriages, so it is supported rather than added. Nothing in the application text or Brief Description says a shape is shown "by way of example" or may take "any closed outline."

No unsupported technical assertion and no verified inconsistency survived the trace, so I am returning an empty findings array.

One thing worth your awareness, outside the scope of findings: no `prior_art/` files were included in this material, and the Background makes only unattributed generic characterizations — the later citation-tracing review will need those files.

Claim 11's installed-assembly class rests on the disclosed clamped-on-pipe state, and method claims 14-17 follow the disclosed install/remove sequence in the disclosed order. Antecedent basis was checked for every claim term. NUMERALS: all 28 entries (10-66) each denote exactly one part, each appears in the detailed description, each appears on at least one sheet, and no numeral is orphaned or reused; the per-figure YAML lists, the "numerals appearing on this sheet" lines, the placement-target lists, and the "Numerals shown" lists agree for all five figures. FIGURES: each brief depicts only disclosed structure. Generic outlines (plain pipe circle, annular frame band, schematic hinge circle, rectangular latch body, plain-block wedge, zigzag springs, rectangular mounting-boss projection, matching-outline segment end faces) are confined to the briefs, are called "shown schematically," and add no taper, angle, depth, slot-end, runout, or proportion statement; no application text or Brief Description sentence says a shape is shown "by way of example" or may have "any closed outline." The one directional statement, that the three oblique slots share one rotational sense, is entailed by the disclosed requirement that a single rotation produce synchronized inward travel of all three carriages. INTERNAL CONSISTENCY: FIG. 3 junction assignments (44/46 at the left hinge-end junction, 48/50 at the right latch-end junction) agree with FIG. 1's left-hinge/right-latch layout and with first-half/upper (12, 32) versus second-half/lower (14, 34); the 1-slot-upper / 2-slot-lower distribution matches carriage placement in FIGS. 1-2; FIG. 4's frame break at the latch end matches FIG. 1; Brief Description entries for FIGS. 1-5 match their briefs; claims, summary, abstract, and description use one consistent set of terms ("ring drive face" for 54 versus "complementary drive faces" for 44-50). No section line is designated in any view, so no cross-view designation conflict arises. No drafting note, placeholder, open question, unresolved alternative, or internal comment remains in the application text. CONTAMINATION CHECK: the drafting agent's own turn asserting a "self-adhering layer with a microsuction surface" is a YOU passage and is not inventor support; no such feature appears anywhere in the title, sections, claims, numerals, or figure briefs. Background prior-art characterizations were not required to trace to the disclosure and were left for the later citation review; note that no prior_art/ files were supplied with this material and the Background makes only unattributed generic characterizations. Every claim limitation, numbered part, figure brief, drawing description, and affirmative inventor source was checked and traced without an unsupported technical assertion or verified internal inconsistency, so the findings array is empty.
